questions.question: In Phase 1 of distributed sort, what do mappers do with their local data?

answers.b: Select random local pivots from their data

explanations.a: Incorrect. Complete sorting happens in Phase 2, not Phase 1.
explanations.b: Correct. In Phase 1, each mapper selects a local pivot (sample) from its data chunk.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Data distribution to reducers happens in Phase 2.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Mappers don't merge with each other in Phase 1.

questions.question: What is the purpose of global pivots in distributed sort?

answers.c: To partition data into balanced buckets across all mappers
answers.d: To eliminate the need for reducers

explanations.a: Incorrect. Global pivots don't directly affect local sorting speed.
explanations.b: Incorrect. While they may help with efficiency, their primary purpose is partitioning.
explanations.c: Correct. Global pivots are used to partition data into buckets that ensure balanced distribution across reducers.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Reducers are still needed to sort their assigned buckets.

questions.question: How does the two-phase approach handle data distribution?

answers.a: Data is randomly distributed among all nodes
answers.b: Data is distributed based on hash values only
answers.c: Data is first sampled for pivots, then distributed based on pivot ranges
answers.d: All data is processed on a single master node

explanations.a: Incorrect. Random distribution doesn't ensure balanced workloads.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Hash-based distribution is a different approach.
explanations.c: Correct. The two-phase approach first samples data to select pivots, then uses these pivots to distribute data.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This would not be a distributed approach.

questions.question: In Phase 2, how do mappers decide which bucket a data element belongs to?

answers.a: Using hash function like hash(value) % reducers
answers.b: Comparing the value against sorted global pivots

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is a different partitioning strategy, not used in pivot-based sorting.
explanations.b: Correct. Mappers compare each data element against the sorted global pivots to determine which bucket it belongs to.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Random assignment would not maintain sort order properties.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Round-robin doesn't consider data values for proper partitioning.

questions.question: What advantage does this two-phase approach have over simple hash partitioning?

answers.c: Better load balancing with unknown data distributions

explanations.a: Incorrect. Execution time depends on various factors, not necessarily faster.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Memory usage is not the primary advantage.
explanations.c: Correct. The two-phase pivot-based approach provides better load balancing because pivots are chosen based on actual data samples.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The two-phase approach is more complex than simple hash partitioning.

questions.question: In the final output, how are the sorted buckets combined?

answers.a: They need to be merged and sorted again
answers.b: They are concatenated in reducer order (naturally sorted)
answers.d: Only the largest bucket is used

explanations.a: Incorrect. No additional sorting is needed if buckets are properly partitioned.
explanations.b: Correct. Since each reducer sorts its bucket locally and buckets are partitioned by global pivots, concatenating in order gives the final sorted output.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Random shuffling would destroy the sort order.
explanations.d: Incorrect. All buckets contribute to the final sorted output.

questions.question: What metric helps measure the efficiency of the distributed sort?

explanations.a: Incorrect. While memory is important, communication overhead is more critical in distributed systems.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Comparison operations are important for algorithmic analysis but not the main distributed efficiency metric.
explanations.c: Correct. Communication rounds measure how much data needs to be transferred between mappers and reducers, which is a key efficiency metric.
explanations.d: Incorrect. File I/O is less critical than network communication in distributed sorting.

questions.question: How does the selection of local pivots affect the overall performance of distributed sort?

answers.a: It has no effect on performance
answers.b: Better pivot selection leads to more balanced data distribution and reduced skew
answers.c: More pivots always result in better performance
answers.d: Pivot selection only affects memory usage

explanations.a: Incorrect. Pivot selection significantly affects performance through load balancing.
explanations.b: Correct. Well-chosen pivots lead to balanced partitions, preventing some reducers from being overloaded while others are idle.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The quality of pivots matters more than quantity; too many pivots can increase overhead.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Pivot selection primarily affects load distribution, not just memory usage.

questions.question: What happens if the data distribution is highly skewed in a distributed sort system?

answers.b: Some reducers may become bottlenecks while others remain underutilized

explanations.a: Incorrect. The algorithm can still work but with reduced efficiency.
explanations.b: Correct. Skewed data can cause load imbalance, where some reducers get much more data than others, creating bottlenecks.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Skewed data typically degrades performance.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Skewed data doesn't necessarily reduce memory usage and may actually increase it on some nodes.
